full_judgment: 4. The respondent No.2 contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition thereto contending, inter alia, that the petitioner has not come with clean hands and he is not entitled to any relief and the Writ Petition involves disputed question of facts, which are required to be proved by adducing oral and documentary evidence and accordingly, the same cannot be adjudicated upon summarily under the writ jurisdiction. None has misappropriated any money from the petitioner; rather, the petitioner in connivance with others received the money of the bank illegally; instead of paying back the money, he filed various criminal cases against the employees of the bank with a mala fide intention to evade the payment. Due to non-co-operation of the petitioner in resolving the matter out of Court, the Board of Directors of the bank was forced to abandon the idea of amicable settlement and demanded the money. Although at the Board meeting the petitioner agreed to pay the entire money he received from the bank illegally, subsequently, he refused to settle the same; rather, he made frivolous claims against the bank. Whether the money received by the petitioner can be converted to forced loan or demand loan can be addressed to in a judicial pronouncement in accordance with the provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and the BRPD Circulars issued from time to time by Bangladesh Bank as decided by a Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No.6395 of 2009. The petitioner did not violate any the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Moreover, the delay is not a bar in filing any suit under the special law, such as, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and, as such, the question of filing an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground of delay is misconceived. However, the defect in filing the suit under section 18(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain may be cured by way of amendment of the plaint at any stage of the trail. Similarly, misjoinder of a party can never be a ground for rejecting a suit under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
